properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: First-party SHA-1 support in the Signal Rust crypto crate: a Digest enum variant (hash.rs parse/update/finalize) plus zkgroup's UUIDv5-style hashing (uid_struct.rs:91), which is specified over SHA-1, and the sha1 crate dependency in Cargo.lock. Changeable here, but UUIDv5 semantics and protocol interop pin this use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls-platform-verifier's Android CertificateVerifier.hashPrincipal() reproduces Android's own X500Principal hash format — first four bytes of the MD5 digest, lowercase hex, reversed, per Chromium's X509Util.java — to build lookup keys for CA subjects in the Android root store. A name-lookup key, not a security digest; the format is dictated by the Android platform and is changeable only by the vendor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: 2 of 21 sites are real non-constant-time comparisons of cryptographic material: the SGX DCAP quote digest check (production, rust/attest/src/dcap/sgx_quote.rs:292 — SHA-256 digest vs QE report data with slice !=) and a zkgroup signature test assert (rust/zkgroup/src/crypto/signature.rs:114). The other 19 were identifier collisions — null-checks on token/hmac fields, cancellation-token enums, FFI buffer checksums, and test string asserts — rejected per site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256-CBC is the Signal protocol's message cipher (unauthenticated CBC; MAC is applied separately per the Signal protocol spec). Sites in aes_cbc.rs:31/42 are the live implementations; lib.rs:16 re-exports them; group_cipher/session_cipher_legacy/triple_ratchet/message-backup/username_links are production call paths; aes_cbc.rs:68-83 are its unit tests of the same functions.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256-CTR is the Signal protocol's v3 wire format: aes_256_ctr_encrypt followed by HMAC-SHA256 over the message (encrypt-then-MAC), so the malleability this class warns about is already addressed by a separate MAC; keystream reuse is prevented by ratchet-derived per-message keys. Sites: rust/protocol/src/crypto.rs message encrypt/decrypt, rust/net/src/svrb.rs forward-secrecy-token encryption (aes_256_ctr_*_hmacsha256), and their tests. The mode is fixed by the wire protocol for compatibility w

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA1 is the legacy Signal protocol message MAC (spec-defined), exposed through the JCE wrapper Mac.java, its Rust counterpart in rust/crypto/src/hash.rs, and tested in CryptographicMacTests. Interop-pinned; sound as a MAC today, deprecated elsewhere.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All confirmed sites are test-only non-cryptographic randomness (random plaintext in GroupCipherTest, PQXDH test bundle factory, SessionBuilderTest test data, Node fixture shuffle); the one SecureRandom site was rejected as a false match (CSPRNG, not weak RNG). No production code uses a non-cryptographic PRNG — production randomness is SecureRandom/OsRng (ALG-80605930).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Poly1305 as the authenticator half of ChaCha20-Poly1305, used in rust/attest's Noise-protocol (snow) handshake resolver for SVR/CDS connections. AEAD as a whole is quantum-adequate (Grover-only); the Poly1305 tag itself is the MAC component.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 is the classical half of Signal's PQXDH hybrid key agreement (paired with Kyber-1024) and underlies the Curve25519 identity/DH ratchet; also used standalone in rust/attest's SNOW resolver (snow_resolver.rs:51 x25519::x25519(privkey, basepoint)). Quantum-vulnerable under Shor — recorded harvestable traffic; the built-in migration is the hybrid itself (and ML-KEM where a pure KEM fits). Declared via curve25519-dalek 5.0 / x25519-dalek 3.0; JNI build sets curve25519_dalek_bits=64. Manifest/a

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 across the codebase: ed25519-dalek dependency, XEdDSA core operations in rust/core/src/curve/curve25519.rs (ED25519_BASEPOINT_TABLE — Signal signs/verifies Curve25519 keys via XEdDSA, i.e. Ed25519), keytrans verifying keys, ED25519 allowed in the TLS signature-algorithm list (tcp_ssl.rs:226), and the vendored Signal Ed25519 certificate (rust/net/src/certs.rs:12, res/signal-ed25519.cer). ed_to_xed.rs is an example exercising the real Ed↔XEd conversion. Shor-vulnerable; migration ML-DSA.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256r1 (X9_62_PRIME256V1) in SGX/DCAP remote-attestation verification: OpenSSL EcGroup for cert-chain and SGX-quote signature verification in rust/attest. fakes.rs sites generate P-256 test certs for the same code path. tcp_ssl.rs:227 permits ECDSA-SECP256R1-SHA256 as a TLS signature algorithm. Algorithm is fixed by Intel's DCAP spec — observable here, replaceable only upstream; still Shor-vulnerable (ECDLP).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 is Signal's signature primitive (prekey signatures, device certificates, SVRB signature chain). Quantum-vulnerable under Shor; migration ML-DSA-65 / SLH-DSA. This object is the lockfile declaration of the implementation the build ships; live call sites are tracked under ALG-5e08bdf5 (Ed25519) and ALG-92e838c9 (P-256) in the other shard.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA (over P-256) used to verify Intel SGX DCAP attestation quotes/certificates: ecdsa_signature_from_bytes parses raw ECDSA signatures from the quote. Algorithm choice is fixed by the Intel DCAP format — observable here, not changeable. Shor-vulnerable signature verification.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.17's X25519 backs the rustls-based TLS connections in the net stack (ECDHE over X25519). Quantum-vulnerable; a hybrid group needs a provider build that offers X25519MLKEM768. The chat connection on BoringSSL is separately configured at rust/net/infra/src/tcp_ssl.rs:240 (ALG-b46aaaf7).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: curve25519-dalek 4.1.3 coexists with the direct 5.0 declaration (Cargo.toml:130) in the locked graph (transitive requirements). Underpins X25519 key agreement and Ed25519 signatures — quantum-vulnerable under Shor.

properties.value: AES-256-GCM is Signal's AEAD (sealed sender v1, message backups, SVRB, device transfer, incremental upload MACs); the Java sites shown are JNI wrappers over the Rust implementation (Native.Aes256Gcm* — construct → update → VerifyTag). 256-bit keys throughout. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Round-3 Kyber-1024, the PQ half of PQXDH prekeys and sealed-sender sessions: production path is KEMKeyPair.generate(KEMKeyType.KYBER_1024) -> Native.KyberKeyPair_Generate and rust kem::KeyType::Kyber1024; parameter set 1024 (~NIST level 5, stronger than the ML-KEM-768 default). Caveat: pre-standard round-3 Kyber, not FIPS 203 ML-KEM (the attest path already uses final ML-KEM via libcrux), so a future parameter/name migration to ML-KEM-1024 is expected but the PQ property holds today. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-256 is the protocol's MAC: the encrypt-then-MAC wire format in rust/protocol/crypto.rs and svrb.rs, account-keys hashing/metadata, the JCE shim (Mac.java admits exactly HMACSha256 and HMACSha1 and delegates to the Rust CryptographicMac), and KAT tests. Strong construction; Grover square-root only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is the workhorse digest: Python build tooling (fetch_archive.py, build_node_bridge.py) verifying artifact checksums; MessageDigest::sha256() as the signing digest for X.509 certs in rust/attest's cert chain and rust/device-transfer; sha2::Sha256 for the SGX quote QE-report digest; and the by-name digest registry in rust/crypto/src/hash.rs. Grover gives only a square-root speedup — sound, not urgent; CNSA 2.0 prefers 384-bit digests for NSS use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ML-KEM-1024 (FIPS 203) via libcrux-ml-kem with the mlkem1024 feature, used in rust/attest's SNOW resolver for post-quantum key agreement with the attestation service; parameter set 1024 rather than the 768 default — CNSA 2.0-aligned strength. Post-quantum safe; this is the migration target the Kyber-1024 sites will eventually converge on.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF-SHA256 is the KDF spine of the Signal protocol: PQXDH shared-secret derivation (protocol/src/pqxdh.rs), ratchet root/chain keys (ratchet/keys.rs), sealed sender (sealed_sender.rs), sender keys, HPKE KDF (rust/crypto/src/hpke/provider.rs), account backup keys (account-keys/backup.rs, message-backup/key.rs), SVR backup (svrb), username-link keys, plus Java/Node/Swift bridge wrappers and their tests, the hkdf crate dependency (Cargo.toml:146) and libcrux-hkdf in about.toml acknowledgments. Qua

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Argon2id PIN hashing for Secure Value Recovery (SVR/SVR2): AccountKeys derives the master key and verifies PINs (rust/account-keys/src/hash.rs, PinHash::create in the SVR2 bridge). Quantum-adequate password KDF; the parameters in hash.rs:53-60 govern its strength.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE2b-512 as the Noise-protocol handshake hash in rust/attest's snow resolver (HashChoice::Blake2b), used for SVR/CDS attested connections. Quantum-adequate (Grover-only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The hmac crate (RustCrypto HMAC construction) in the lockfile — the implementation behind the HMAC-SHA1/HMAC-SHA256 usage in rust/crypto and the protocol's message MACs. Dependency inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2 provides SHA-256/384/512 used for digests, HKDF, HMAC and the attest path; Grover gives only a square-root speedup so hashes are not urgent, but CNSA 2.0 wants 384-bit digests for NSS use. Call sites live under ALG-695a1eb5 (SHA-256) and ALG-8c748911 (SHA-384/512).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-512 throughout: XEdDSA/Ed25519 internals (curve25519.rs — spec-required), the Digest enum's SHA-512 variant (rust/crypto hash.rs), key-transparency VRF hashing, safety-number fingerprints (protocol/fingerprint.rs), SVR backup (svrb), and username hashing (usernames). Meets CNSA 2.0 digest size.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The AES-256 family is Signal's symmetric cipher surface across all bridges: Aes256Ctr32 (legacy keystream), AES-256-GCM streaming encrypt/decrypt (Aes256GcmEncryption/Decryption), Aes256GcmSiv (sealed-sender auth tags in rust/protocol, zkgroup group params), exposed over JNI (Native.kt), the Node N-API (node/ts/index.ts Aes256GcmSiv) and Swift, with tests per platform. Grover leaves a 128-bit margin; no change needed for PQ.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CSPRNG inventory: production randomness is java.security.SecureRandom (message-backup BackupKey byte derivation) and the Rust rand stack (OsRng-backed csprng seen feeding every KEM/ECDH keygen in the protocol crates' tests and benches); test files wrap SecureRandom with fixed seeds (createSecureRandom(SEED)) for determinism. Posture control: strong RNG in production paths; the weak-RNG sightings elsewhere in the inventory are test-only (ALG-7d1fdc12).

Parsing only — selects no weak algorithm.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: chacha20poly1305 crate: the AEAD used in the Noise (snow) handshake resolver in rust/attest for CDS/SVR connections, plus the ChaCha20-Poly1305/Poly1305 algorithm objects ALG-3d4cff53/ALG-e6238d01 record the same use sites. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The ring crypto library: used in rust/net/infra/src/certs.rs for certificate/key handling in the network stack, and the likely default provider behind rustls. ring does not offer post-quantum key exchange (no ML-KEM as of the locked version), so TLS sessions built on it negotiate classical groups only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto aes-gcm crate — the AEAD implementation behind the HPKE provider (rust/crypto/src/hpke/provider.rs) and the AES-256-GCM sites tracked under ALG-f61ec50f. Symmetric AE, quantum-safe. Available in the shipped library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ed25519-dalek — the Ed25519 implementation this build ships; used in rust/keytrans (key-transparency signature verification) and the protocol's prekey/device-certificate signatures. Quantum-vulnerable under Shor; migration ML-DSA-65 / SLH-DSA. Same dependency as ALG-683d5cd2 (lockfile facet).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls TLS stack, declared in the workspace Cargo.toml and rust/bridge/jni/impl/Cargo.toml (the Android platform-verifier bridge). TLS 1.3 sessions ride on it; PQ readiness depends on the rustls version (0.23.45 per lockfile) and its crypto provider (ring has no ML-KEM; X25519MLKEM768 needs aws-lc-rs). No explicit kx-group configuration was found in the tree, so sessions negotiate provider-default classical groups.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The sha2 crate: SHA-256/SHA-512 digests across 11 files (account-keys MFA metadata, attest DCAP evidence, incremental MAC types, curve25519 internals, etc.) — the digest workhorse behind HKDF, fingerprints, and XEdDSA.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS 1.3 protocol support via rustls 0.23.45. Protocol configuration asset: TLS 1.3 key exchange with a rustls 0.23 + ring provider is classical (X25519/secp256r1) — harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure on every rustls-backed connection unless a hybrid group (X25519MLKEM768) is enabled via an aws-lc-rs build. No kx-group override was found in the tree; group selection is provider-default.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto argon2 crate — Argon2id memory-hard KDF used by rust/account-keys for PIN-derived account secrets (registration/recovery). Password KDF, not quantum-relevant (no Shor speedup); its security rests on the memory-hardness parameters, recorded under ALG-d75ee937.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: x25519-dalek: the X25519 implementation behind the Signal protocol's ECDH (X25519 in PQXDH hybrid with ML-KEM, ratchet chain, sealed sender). The X25519 algorithm itself is Shor-vulnerable; its migration is ML-KEM-768, which the protocol already layers on top in PQXDH. Algorithm use is recorded under the X25519 object (ALG-1138d04b); this entry records the implementation dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto sha1 crate — the SHA-1 implementation backing the SHA-1 sites under ALG-725ecd3e. SHA-1 is collision-broken; retained where it exists for legacy-format compatibility (zkgroup uid hashing / crypto hash module — see scout 1's site verdicts for purpose).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto hmac crate — implements the HMAC-SHA-256 / HMAC-SHA-1 constructions used throughout the protocol (ALG-ce74cadc, ALG-ba399e5b) and the svrb/crypto.rs encrypt-then-MAC paths. MAC construction; Grover-weakened only, not urgent.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: curve25519-dalek@4.1.3 — the Curve25519 field-arithmetic library (transitive 4.x line) underpinning X25519 key agreement and Ed25519 signatures; quantum-vulnerable under Shor. Same lockfile asset as ALG-82f1eeb2.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: zkgroup AuthCredentialWithPni: a server-issued, blind-signed group auth credential (presented anonymously with GroupSecretParams — the group's secret scalar — and fresh randomness). Real cryptographic credential material handled here, not a hardcoded literal; the secret-named variable is a parameter of the presentation path. Part of the zkgroup zero-knowledge credential system.
